name: When should I consider a full roof replacement versus a repair?

mainEntity.name: When should I consider a full roof replacement versus a repair?

acceptedAnswer.text: You should consider a full roof replacement when your roof is nearing the end of its lifespan, typically 20-25 years for asphalt shingles, or if there's extensive damage. If damage is localized to a small area, a repair might suffice. However, widespread shingle damage, significant leaks in multiple spots, or structural issues often indicate that a full replacement is more cost-effective and provides better long-term protection. An inspection by a professional can accurately assess the extent of damage and help you make an informed decision.
acceptedAnswer.description: Consider a full replacement when your roof is old or has extensive damage; localized issues might allow for a repair, but a professional inspection is key.
